findings.reason: part 1 of the existing deliverable moves a request ahead of the ranked walk to avoid a delay it does not actually incur, so a node would implement queue-jumping and could never show the stall it was written for.
findings.text: s21 says a request released from awaiting-upstream "waits for the rest of its pass's launch stage, which ran 1,200–4,000 s that day", but `admit_once` calls `advance_waiting_requests(live)` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3683) before it builds its queued list from the same `live` objects, and `_resolve_and_move` mutates the pointer's phase in place (2711-2739) while `_move_pointer` leaves `queued_at` untouched (3196-3213), so the released request is in that pass's queue walk at its original queue rank and is launched there, not on a later pass; the 1,200–4,000 s the section cites is the pass's `launch_seconds`, which s4 attributes to wait resolution inside the same pass

findings.reason: a node implementing the shortcut inside `require_plan_reviewed` would leave the per-launch `review_coverage` calls untouched, so the section's first done-when ("calls review_coverage zero times") would fail after the work was done in the place the plan named.
findings.text: s4's deliverable says the launch-time reuse happens in `require_plan_reviewed` ("compares those digests with the plan's present ones and returns at once when neither moved"), but a queued request reaches the launch through `_plan_review_owed` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3244), which already compares the stored contract digests (`REVIEW_CONTRACT_KEY`, 3296-3339) and calls `plan_review.review_coverage` for every request on every pass with no per-pass cache; `routing.require_plan_reviewed` is reached only for a pointer with no current contract, through `_dispatch_gate_owed` (3216-3236)

findings.reason: the case as worded and the control cannot both fail on the same defect, so a node can land all three parts with part 3 (the reader fallback) dead and still see the declared control pass.
findings.text: s19's first case asks for a request "whose stored waits gain a run: ref through `_rederive_waits`, with that ref absent from `wait_projects`", and its negative control restores `or ""` in `_wait_state`; but the section's own part 2 makes `_rederive_waits` write `wait_projects` in the same pointer mutation that writes the waits (the `_rederive_waits` rewrite at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2930-2945 writes only `waits` and `waits_at` today), so once the writer is fixed a ref that "gains" through `_rederive_waits` can no longer be absent from `wait_projects`, and the first case passes through the writer while the restored `or ""` is never consulted
